title: Nitsche methods for weak boundary enforcement

items.title: Restriction Sobolev spaces for Nitsche analysis
items.strategy: Define H^s on a bounded polyhedral set as the restriction space with its quotient Bessel-potential norm, fixing the convention needed for fractional boundary traces.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Chapter 37, Nitsche boundary penalty method

items.title: Zero facet traces of functions in H1_0 on an affine mesh
items.strategy: Pull back the reference-simplex trace map to each cell and pass the zero restrictions of a Countable-Choice-selected compactly supported smooth approximating sequence to the trace limit.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Chapter 37, Nitsche boundary penalty method
Mika Juntunen and Rolf Stenberg, Nitsche's method for general boundary conditions, Mathematics of Computation 78 (2009), 1353–1374

items.title: Local inverse trace bound for a polynomial normal flux
items.strategy: Apply the published polynomial facet trace estimate to each component of the cellwise gradient and use the shape-regular equivalence of face height and cell diameter.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Chapter 37, Nitsche boundary penalty method
Mika Juntunen and Rolf Stenberg, Nitsche's method for general boundary conditions, Mathematics of Computation 78 (2009), 1353–1374

items.title: Fractional Sobolev traces on simplex facets
items.strategy: Prove the H^s-to-L2 hyperplane trace inequality by Fourier slicing for s>1/2 and descend to the quotient restriction space using locality.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Chapter 37, Nitsche boundary penalty method
Mika Juntunen and Rolf Stenberg, Nitsche's method for general boundary conditions, Mathematics of Computation 78 (2009), 1353–1374

items.title: Symmetric and nonsymmetric Nitsche boundary forms
items.strategy: Define the full H1-conforming polynomial trial space, boundary face scale, weak Dirichlet penalty, and the two consistent forms with the source's sign convention.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Chapter 37, Nitsche boundary penalty method
Mika Juntunen and Rolf Stenberg, Nitsche's method for general boundary conditions, Mathematics of Computation 78 (2009), 1353–1374

items.title: Global boundary-flux estimate on a matching mesh
items.strategy: Sum the local inverse trace bounds and count the boundary facets incident to each cell, then apply weighted Cauchy–Schwarz.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Chapter 37, Nitsche boundary penalty method
Mika Juntunen and Rolf Stenberg, Nitsche's method for general boundary conditions, Mathematics of Computation 78 (2009), 1353–1374

items.title: Nitsche coercivity above the inverse-trace threshold
items.strategy: Bound the consistency cross term by the global flux constant and compute the smallest eigenvalue of the resulting two-variable quadratic form for each symmetry parameter.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Chapter 37, Nitsche boundary penalty method
Mika Juntunen and Rolf Stenberg, Nitsche's method for general boundary conditions, Mathematics of Computation 78 (2009), 1353–1374

items.title: Nitsche consistency and energy quasi-optimality
items.strategy: Use the local Green identity to obtain exact consistency, prove finite-dimensional solvability from coercivity, and derive the zero-residual affine Strang bound directly from discrete coercivity and boundedness.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Chapter 37, Nitsche boundary penalty method
Mika Juntunen and Rolf Stenberg, Nitsche's method for general boundary conditions, Mathematics of Computation 78 (2009), 1353–1374

items.title: Nonsymmetric Nitsche L2 estimate with its boundary consistency defect
items.strategy: Use the zero-trace discrete test approximation in the adjoint identity; the nonsymmetric form leaves the exact boundary flux term, which is bounded by the boundary penalty norm and the dual trace estimate.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Chapter 37, Nitsche boundary penalty method
Mika Juntunen and Rolf Stenberg, Nitsche's method for general boundary conditions, Mathematics of Computation 78 (2009), 1353–1374

items.title: Symmetric Nitsche L2 estimate under dual regularity and Nitsche approximation
items.strategy: Solve the adjoint Poisson problem, use symmetric adjoint consistency to cancel the boundary residual, subtract a zero-trace discrete approximant, and apply the stated Nitsche comparison-norm approximation bound.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Chapter 37, Nitsche boundary penalty method
Mika Juntunen and Rolf Stenberg, Nitsche's method for general boundary conditions, Mathematics of Computation 78 (2009), 1353–1374

title: Nitsche methods for weak boundary enforcement — Examples

items.title: Exact affine data under weak imposition
items.strategy: Substitute the exact affine solution into each Nitsche form and compare with strong imposition on the zero-trace subspace.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Chapter 37, Nitsche boundary penalty method
Mika Juntunen and Rolf Stenberg, Nitsche's method for general boundary conditions, Mathematics of Computation 78 (2009), 1353–1374

items.title: Penalties below and above the Nitsche coercivity threshold
items.strategy: Compute the penalty-free constant-mode failure and apply the proven sufficient threshold to the same finite-element model.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Chapter 37, Nitsche boundary penalty method
Mika Juntunen and Rolf Stenberg, Nitsche's method for general boundary conditions, Mathematics of Computation 78 (2009), 1353–1374

items.title: The symmetric cancellation and nonsymmetric L2 boundary defect
items.strategy: Write the duality identities for both signs and isolate the boundary-flux term that cancels only in the symmetric form.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Chapter 37, Nitsche boundary penalty method
Mika Juntunen and Rolf Stenberg, Nitsche's method for general boundary conditions, Mathematics of Computation 78 (2009), 1353–1374
